summary: Nora no longer reads a source's silence as a denial. If what she checked doesn't cover the question, she says she couldn't check — instead of concluding the thing doesn't exist and taking back an answer she'd already found and sourced.
details: The real failure this closes: she'd established a fact from a source that covered it and said so with attribution; two minutes later a search returned an article scoped to only one category of the thing being asked about, and she read its silence about the rest as proof there was nothing there — overturning her own correct answer. The article wasn't wrong, it was narrower than the question. Her doctrine already told an empty result apart from a broken lookup; it had nothing for a source that simply doesn't cover the question, and that third case now routes to the same honest 'I couldn't check' the broken lookup gets.

The rule that messages are things to reason about and never orders now covers every block she's handed — what people typed, what she remembers about them, how the room talks, what a lookup brought back — including any block added later. It previously named only two of the eight, leaving everything she remembers outside it.

Restores the half of her anti-capitulation rule that governs how a concession or a refusal SOUNDS — how she takes a correction, and how she holds an answer she actually looked up. It was removed in two steps back in August, along with the test that guarded it, and had been gone for over five days when she caved; the other half was present only in its thinnest form. It is written as part of her portrait rather than as a rule, which is how the file it lives in is written.
limitations: The non-coverage rule is doctrine prose, and prose alone has repeatedly failed to move this class of behaviour. Its eval corpus (evals/adversarial/source_scope.yaml) is a measured record of the gap, deliberately not wired in as a passing gate — the structural fix is the separate reasoning-continuity work.
